reason: A dispatches at most one waiting customer per loop iteration, so after an inline zero-length Finish it stalls or terminates early with customers still queued (violating R6/R13/R15), whereas B keeps dispatching FIFO at the same tick.

A expands each expression before validating later syntax (violating R5) and, like D, wrongly emits UnsupportedOperator for non-operator punctuation, while C reports InvalidName instead of EmptyVariable for a leading comma; B follows R5-R11 precedence exactly.
Only C traverses the normalized cwd/home components through the link table before the request components as R31 requires; A and B start from the context stack without link lookups.

A reports caret/tilde partial-validation and overflow errors at the token start instead of the operand start, and C silently drops bare-partial upper-bound overflow and reports all-wildcard caret/tilde at the operand rather than token start, while B matches R25/R29/R32.
B and C parse the port before validating the host, violating the R3 host-then-port error order (e.g. an empty host with a bad port), while A validates host first.
A never rounds up (its threshold is (r+1)^2) and caps its sqrt search at 3e9, failing non-square and large edges, whereas C (functionally identical to B) rounds correctly using exact u128 isqrt.

B returns set_capacity evictions best-to-worst instead of worst-to-best (R43), and C is correct like A and D but with the cheapest per-operation cost (swap_remove with index fix-up instead of full sorts or index rebuilds).

B returns UnclosedQuote or accepts input where R10 requires TrailingLocal after the closing quote, and C makes parse_email non-public and reports empty labels before fully validating earlier labels (violating R16/R21), while A follows the specified precedence.

A never checks that bases are digits-only, so starred range endpoints like *-5 or 5-* explicitly required by R8 to be InvalidSyntax panic or misreport, while B validates base structure first and only misplaces numeric offsets for non-first list items.
